$comment: What scripts/measure-edit-to-view.cs holds each target to, in milliseconds: the warm median of each
part named, and the run fails over it (#900). The roadmap's bar is a second. The desktop meets it and
is held to it. The web does not, by tens of seconds, so its total is held to a CEILING that only comes
down: set from the first CI run that measured it (a warm median of 22.9s, its warm runs 22.9 to 39.2s)
with room for the runner's spread. Each slice of #900 lowers it by what it measured, and the run says
when the median falls under half of it. #1274 took 0.5s off the wait after a save (553ms on CI, under
100ms after it), and #1276 took the MSBuild part off a save (6.8s on CI, a few milliseconds after it). #1278 took
1.9s off eqc's part, its median from 5.5s at a load average of 35 to 38 to 3.6s at 27 to 31.
#1280 kept one bun between saves and wrote only what changed: bun's part from a median of 508ms (its
runs 261 to 1230ms, a load average of 198 to 235) to 145ms (77 to 439ms, at 147 to 204). It lowers the
ceiling by 0.3s, under the 0.36s it measured, since the two ran at different loads.
